words.enDefinition: to heat the oven to the required temperature before putting food in it

examples.en: I forgot to preheat the oven before mixing the batter for the muffins.
examples.zh: 我调松饼面糊之前，忘了「预热烤箱」。

examples.en: The recipe says to preheat the oven while getting the vegetables ready.
examples.zh: 食谱说，准备蔬菜时要「预热烤箱」。

collocations: preheat the oven to the required temperature

words.enDefinition: a selected function or operating mode on an oven

examples.en: I checked which oven setting the recipe used before putting the tray inside.
examples.zh: 把烤盘放进去前，我查了一下食谱选的是哪种「烤箱模式」。

examples.en: The person who owns our flat showed me the oven setting for ordinary baking.
examples.zh: 房东给我看了普通烘烤用的是哪种「烤箱模式」。

words.enDefinition: an oven that heats food without using a fan to circulate hot air

examples.en: Our conventional oven browned the vegetables more quickly on the upper rack.
examples.zh: 我们的「无风扇传统烤箱」上层烤架上的蔬菜更快上色。

examples.en: The recipe lists a separate temperature for people using a conventional oven.
examples.zh: 食谱为用「无风扇传统烤箱」的人单列了一个温度。

words.enDefinition: a numbered oven-temperature setting used in British recipes and on some gas ovens

examples.en: The recipe gave a gas mark instead of a temperature in degrees.
examples.zh: 食谱用「燃气烤箱温度档」表示火力，没有写多少度。

examples.en: I checked which gas mark the dial was showing before baking the rolls.
examples.zh: 烤面包卷之前，我核对了旋钮指在哪个「燃气烤箱温度档」。

collocations: set the oven to gas mark four

words.enDefinition: the height at which an oven rack is placed inside the oven

examples.en: I changed the rack position so the top of the loaf would brown evenly.
examples.zh: 我调整了「烤架层位」，让面包顶部均匀上色。

examples.en: The manual shows the recommended rack position for baking with two trays.
examples.zh: 说明书标出了同时用两个烤盘时建议的「烤架层位」。

words.enDefinition: to make the temperature or power of a cooking heat source lower

examples.en: I went back to reduce the heat once the soup started bubbling steadily.
examples.zh: 汤开始持续冒泡后，我回去「调低火力」。

examples.en: The recipe says to reduce the heat after the water comes to a boil.
examples.zh: 食谱说，水烧开后要「调低火力」。

words.enDefinition: a cooking heat setting between low and high

examples.en: I cooked the vegetables over medium heat while my flatmate prepared the rice.
examples.zh: 我用「中火」做蔬菜，室友在旁边准备米饭。

examples.en: The recipe asks for medium heat so the onions soften without browning quickly.
examples.zh: 食谱要求用「中火」，让洋葱软下来，同时别太快变褐。

collocations: set the pan over medium heat

words.enDefinition: a cooking setting hotter than medium but below the strongest setting

examples.en: I used medium-high heat to brown the mushrooms in the shared kitchen.
examples.zh: 我在共用厨房用「中大火」把蘑菇煎到上色。

examples.en: The pan was already over medium-high heat when I added the vegetables.
examples.zh: 我放蔬菜时，锅已经是「中大火」在加热。

collocations: heat a pan over medium-high heat

words.enDefinition: a gentle cooking setting that supplies relatively little heat

examples.en: I kept the sauce over low heat while the others set the table.
examples.zh: 其他人摆餐具时，我让酱汁用「小火」继续加热。

examples.en: The recipe used low heat to melt the butter without browning it.
examples.zh: 食谱用「小火」把黄油融化，同时不让它变褐。

words.enDefinition: cooking heat applied straight to food from a flame, hot surface or element

examples.en: I moved the vegetables off the direct heat when the edges browned.
examples.zh: 蔬菜边缘上色后，我把它们从「直接受热」的位置移开。

examples.en: The grill has one area for direct heat and another for slower cooking.
examples.zh: 烧烤架一处可以「直接受热」，另一处能慢慢烤。

collocations: move food away from direct heat

words.enDefinition: heat that reaches food from around it rather than from directly underneath or above

examples.en: The recipe uses indirect heat to cook the vegetables more gently on the grill.
examples.zh: 食谱让蔬菜在烤架上「间接受热」，这样火候更柔和。

examples.en: I asked which side of the grill was set up for indirect heat.
examples.zh: 我问烧烤架哪一侧设成了「间接受热」区。

words.enDefinition: to heat a liquid until it begins to boil

examples.en: The instructions said to bring to a boil before adding the rice.
examples.zh: 盒子上的说明是，先把水「加热至沸腾」，再放米。

examples.en: The soup recipe uses the phrase bring to a boil before the simmering step.
examples.zh: 汤的食谱在小火慢煮之前写了「加热至沸腾」。

collocations: bring to a boil over medium heat
bring to a boil while stirring

words.enDefinition: a vigorous boil with large bubbles rising continuously across the liquid's surface

examples.en: The water reached a rolling boil while I took the pasta from the cupboard.
examples.zh: 我从柜子里拿意面的时候，水已经「持续剧烈沸腾」了。

examples.en: I waited for a rolling boil before following the next part of the recipe.
examples.zh: 我等到水「持续剧烈沸腾」，才按食谱做下一步。

collocations: bring water to a rolling boil
keep water at a rolling boil

words.enDefinition: to boil so vigorously that liquid or foam spills out of the container

examples.en: I took the lid off when the pasta water began to boil over.
examples.zh: 煮意面的水开始「沸腾溢出」时，我掀开了锅盖。

examples.en: My flatmate saw the milk boil over while I was setting the table.
examples.zh: 我摆餐具时，室友看到牛奶「沸腾溢出」。

collocations: watch for liquid that may boil over

words.enDefinition: to cook in liquid kept just below or at a very gentle boil

examples.en: I left the sauce to simmer while chopping the herbs for dinner.
examples.zh: 我让酱汁「小火慢煮」，同时切好晚餐用的香草。

examples.en: The soup can simmer while we prepare the plates for our guests.
examples.zh: 我们给客人摆盘时，可以让汤继续「小火慢煮」。

words.enDefinition: to cook a liquid at a gentle simmer without covering its container

examples.en: The recipe asked me to simmer uncovered so the sauce could thicken.
examples.zh: 食谱要求「不盖锅盖小火慢煮」，让酱汁收浓。

examples.en: I left the soup to simmer uncovered while the bread finished warming.
examples.zh: 面包加热好之前，我让汤「不盖锅盖小火慢煮」。

collocations: leave a sauce to simmer uncovered

words.enDefinition: to cook food gently in hot liquid with little or no bubbling

examples.en: We planned to poach the pears for dessert after our group dinner.
examples.zh: 我们计划聚餐后做甜点，把梨「用热液低温浸煮」熟。

examples.en: The cook explained why she chose to poach the fish in the demonstration.
examples.zh: 厨师说明了示范时为什么选择把鱼「用热液低温浸煮」。

words.enDefinition: to boil an egg so that the yolk remains soft

examples.en: I wanted to soft-boil the eggs for breakfast in our shared kitchen.
examples.zh: 我想在共用厨房做早餐，把鸡蛋「煮成溏心」。

examples.en: My flatmate chose to soft-boil an egg for the noodle bowl.
examples.zh: 室友决定把鸡蛋「煮成溏心」，放进汤面里。

words.enDefinition: to boil an egg until both its white and yolk are firm

examples.en: I planned to hard-boil some eggs for the lunches we were packing.
examples.zh: 我们正准备带出门的午饭，我打算「把一些鸡蛋煮熟透」。

examples.en: The recipe says to hard-boil the eggs before adding them to the salad.
examples.zh: 食谱说，先「把鸡蛋煮熟透」，再放进沙拉。

words.enDefinition: to cook vegetables using steam without putting them directly in water

examples.en: I decided to steam the vegetables while my flatmate prepared the noodles.
examples.zh: 室友准备面条时，我决定「用蒸汽蒸蔬菜」。

examples.en: The recipe says to steam the vegetables before tossing them in the dressing.
examples.zh: 食谱说，拌调味汁之前先「用蒸汽蒸蔬菜」。

collocations: steam the vegetables in a basket

words.enDefinition: to cook something briefly in boiling water, often followed by cooling

examples.en: The recipe says to blanch the beans before adding them to the salad.
examples.zh: 食谱说，先把豆角「短时焯水」，再加进沙拉。

examples.en: In the class, we watched the cook blanch vegetables for a cold dish.
examples.zh: 课上，我们看厨师为做凉菜而把蔬菜「短时焯水」。

words.enDefinition: to cook food partly by boiling it before finishing it another way

examples.en: I decided to parboil the potatoes before putting them in the roasting tray.
examples.zh: 我决定先把土豆「预煮至半熟」，再放进烤盘。

examples.en: The recipe suggests that we parboil the carrots before finishing them in the oven.
examples.zh: 食谱建议先把胡萝卜「预煮至半熟」，再用烤箱烤到熟。

words.enDefinition: to bake a pastry case before putting its filling into it

examples.en: I needed to blind bake the pastry case before adding the lemon filling.
examples.zh: 加柠檬馅前，我需要先「空烤派皮」。

examples.en: The instructor showed us how to blind bake a tart shell in class.
examples.zh: 讲师在课堂上示范了怎样「空烤派皮」。

words.enDefinition: to bake something partway, so it can be finished in the oven later

examples.en: We had to parbake the pizza bases before adding the toppings for dinner.
examples.zh: 我们给晚饭做比萨，要先把饼底「预烤至半熟」，再放配料。

examples.en: The bakery uses the word parbake for rolls that customers finish at home.
examples.zh: 面包店用「预烤至半熟」来形容顾客要回家烤透的面包卷。

words.enDefinition: to cook food using dry heat, typically in an oven

examples.en: We decided to roast the vegetables while the rice was cooking on the hob.
examples.zh: 我们决定趁炉子上煮饭时，把蔬菜「用干热烘烤」。

examples.en: The recipe asks you to roast the pumpkin before adding it to the soup.
examples.zh: 食谱要求南瓜先「用干热烘烤」，再加到汤里。

words.enDefinition: to roast food at a relatively low temperature for a long time

examples.en: My flatmate wanted to slow-roast the tomatoes for our sauce on Sunday.
examples.zh: 室友想周日把番茄「低温慢烤」，用来做酱汁。

examples.en: The recipe uses the term slow-roast for the vegetables in the main dish.
examples.zh: 食谱把主菜蔬菜的烹法称为「低温慢烤」。

words.enDefinition: to use dry heat to brown food lightly and bring out its flavour

examples.en: I wanted to toast the sesame seeds before sprinkling them on our salad.
examples.zh: 我打算先把芝麻「烘烤至褐香」，再撒到沙拉上。

examples.en: We used the same pan to toast the bread for the soup.
examples.zh: 我们用同一个锅把配汤的面包「烘烤至褐香」。

words.enDefinition: to heat food until browned or fragrant without adding oil or other liquid

examples.en: I planned to dry-roast the cumin seeds before mixing them into the sauce.
examples.zh: 我打算先把孜然籽「无油干烘」，再拌进酱汁。

examples.en: The recipe asks cooks to dry-roast the nuts for the salad topping.
examples.zh: 食谱要求先把撒在沙拉上的坚果「无油干烘」。

words.enDefinition: to cook food using strong direct heat from above or below

examples.en: We decided to grill the peppers for the sandwiches at our weekend lunch.
examples.zh: 我们决定把甜椒「烤一下」，夹进周末午饭的三明治里。

examples.en: The British recipe says to grill the cheese under the oven's top element.
examples.zh: 那份英国食谱说，把奶酪放在烤箱顶部的加热元件下面「烤」。

words.enDefinition: dark lines left on food where it touched the hot bars of a grill

examples.en: The aubergine had clear grill marks after we turned each piece over.
examples.zh: 茄子一片片翻面后，能看到清楚的「烤架焦纹」。

examples.en: My flatmate noticed the grill marks before taking the peppers off the rack.
examples.zh: 室友先看到了「烤架焦纹」，然后才把甜椒从烤架上拿下来。

words.enDefinition: to cook food in a frying pan with a small amount of fat

examples.en: I decided to pan-fry the halloumi for the sandwiches after our morning class.
examples.zh: 上午下课后，我决定「用平底锅煎」哈罗米奶酪来做三明治。

examples.en: The recipe explains how to pan-fry the onions before adding the remaining vegetables.
examples.zh: 食谱说明了加其他蔬菜之前，怎样「用平底锅煎」洋葱。

words.enDefinition: to fry food in oil that comes partway up its sides without covering it

examples.en: Our instructor showed us how to shallow-fry the fritters in a wide pan.
examples.zh: 老师用一个宽平底锅，示范怎样给炸饼「浅油煎炸」。

examples.en: The recipe says to shallow-fry the cakes until both sides are crisp.
examples.zh: 食谱说，把饼「浅油煎炸」，直到两面变脆。

words.enDefinition: to cook food fully immersed in hot oil

examples.en: The cook decided to deep-fry the potato strips for the café's lunch service.
examples.zh: 厨师决定把午餐要卖的土豆条「浸油炸」。

examples.en: We watched the chef deep-fry dough pieces during a demonstration at college.
examples.zh: 我们在学院的演示课上看厨师把小面团「浸油炸」。

words.enDefinition: to cook small pieces of food quickly over high heat while stirring

examples.en: I used the wok to stir-fry greens for dinner in our shared kitchen.
examples.zh: 我在共用厨房用炒锅「翻炒」绿叶菜做晚饭。

examples.en: The recipe asks you to stir-fry the vegetables before adding the sauce.
examples.zh: 食谱要求先「翻炒」蔬菜，再加酱汁。

words.enDefinition: to cook food quickly in a small amount of fat over fairly high heat

examples.en: I used a small pan to sauté mushrooms for the toast at breakfast.
examples.zh: 我用小平底锅「用少量油快炒」蘑菇，早餐配吐司吃。

examples.en: The recipe says to sauté the garlic briefly before adding the tomatoes.
examples.zh: 食谱说，先把蒜「用少量油快炒」一下，再加番茄。

words.enDefinition: to cook onions gently in a little fat until soft without browning them

examples.en: I began to sweat the onions while my roommate prepared the vegetable stock.
examples.zh: 我开始「小火炒软洋葱」，室友在旁边准备蔬菜高汤。

examples.en: The instructor said to sweat the onions before adding the rice to the pan.
examples.zh: 老师说，要先「小火炒软洋葱」，再把米倒进锅里。

collocations: sweat the onions over low heat
sweat the onions without browning them

words.enDefinition: to expose food to strong heat briefly so its surface browns

examples.en: I watched the cook sear the tofu before adding it to the sauce.
examples.zh: 我看厨师先把豆腐「高温煎至表面上色」，再放进酱汁。

examples.en: The demonstration showed how to sear the outside without cooking the whole piece through.
examples.zh: 示范展示了怎样只「高温煎至表面上色」，同时不让整块食材熟透。

collocations: quickly sear a piece of fish

words.enDefinition: to cook meat until its outside turns brown, often before another cooking step

examples.en: The recipe asks us to brown the meat before adding the other ingredients.
examples.zh: 食谱要求先「把肉表面煎上色」，再加其他配料。

examples.en: My flatmate offered to brown the meat while I chopped the carrots.
examples.zh: 室友主动帮我「把肉表面煎上色」，我来切胡萝卜。

collocations: brown the meat on all sides

words.enDefinition: to cook onions until they become sweet and deep golden brown

examples.en: I began to caramelize the onions for our sandwiches while the bread warmed.
examples.zh: 面包加热时，我开始「把洋葱炒到焦糖色」，准备夹三明治。

examples.en: The recipe says to caramelize the onions before stirring them into the lentils.
examples.zh: 食谱说，先「把洋葱炒到焦糖色」，再拌进扁豆里。

collocations: caramelize the onions for a topping

words.enDefinition: to cause a liquid or moisture to evaporate by continuing to heat it

examples.en: The recipe says to cook off any excess water before adding the seasoning.
examples.zh: 食谱说，调味前要「加热使多余的水分蒸发」。

examples.en: I left the mixture on the stove to cook off some liquid.
examples.zh: 我把混合物继续放在炉子上，「加热使一部分液体蒸发」。

words.enDefinition: to fry small groups of food one at a time instead of all together

examples.en: I had to fry in batches because our pan was too small.
examples.zh: 我们的平底锅太小，我只好「分批煎炸」。

examples.en: The cook chose to fry in batches so the pieces would not crowd the pan.
examples.zh: 厨师选择「分批煎炸」，这样锅里放的食材不会太挤。

collocations: fry in batches to avoid crowding
fry in batches in the same pan

words.enDefinition: to turn food over midway through its cooking time

examples.en: The recipe says to turn halfway through so each side has time to brown.
examples.zh: 食谱说要「做到一半时翻面」，这样两面都有时间上色。

examples.en: My flatmate reminded me to turn halfway through when we roasted the wedges.
examples.zh: 我们烤薯角时，室友提醒我「做到一半时翻面」。

collocations: turn halfway through the cooking time

words.enDefinition: fat and juices left in a pan after cooking meat or other food

examples.en: My roommate used the pan drippings to make gravy for our Sunday lunch.
examples.zh: 室友用「锅底肉汁和油脂」做肉汁酱，配周日午饭。

examples.en: The recipe asks you to keep the pan drippings after removing the roast.
examples.zh: 食谱要求取出烤肉后保留「锅底肉汁和油脂」。

collocations: skim fat from the pan drippings

words.zhGloss: 用液体溶开锅底焦香残渣
words.enDefinition: to add liquid to a hot pan to loosen and dissolve browned bits
acceptedZhAnswers: 用液体溶开锅底焦香残渣

examples.en: I used a little stock to deglaze the pan after cooking the mushrooms.
examples.zh: 做完蘑菇后，我用了少量高汤「溶解锅底焦褐残渣」。

examples.en: The instructor explained why she would deglaze the pan before making the sauce.
examples.zh: 老师解释了做酱汁前为什么要「用液体溶开锅底焦香残渣」。

collocations: deglaze the pan for a sauce

words.enDefinition: a sauce made in the same pan as a cooked item, often using its browned residue

examples.en: I made a simple pan sauce while the cooked pieces rested on a plate.
examples.zh: 煎好的食材在盘子里静置时，我做了个简单的「锅汁酱」。

examples.en: The pan sauce picked up the flavour of the mushrooms and herbs.
examples.zh: 「锅汁酱」带上了蘑菇和香草的味道。

words.enDefinition: to spoon or brush fat or liquid over food during cooking

examples.en: The chef stopped to baste the roast before returning it to the oven.
examples.zh: 厨师先「将油汁浇在烤肉上」，再把肉送回烤箱。

examples.en: I saw my flatmate baste the vegetables with oil from the tray.
examples.zh: 我看到室友把「烤盘里的油浇在蔬菜上」。

words.enDefinition: to coat a pan with a small amount of cooking oil

examples.en: I remembered to lightly oil the pan before adding the first pancake.
examples.zh: 放第一张薄饼前，我记得「在锅里薄薄抹油」。

examples.en: The recipe says to lightly oil the pan so the cakes lift easily.
examples.zh: 食谱说要「在锅里薄薄抹油」，这样饼比较容易铲起来。

collocations: lightly oil the pan before cooking
lightly oil the pan with a brush
make sure to lightly oil the pan

words.enDefinition: to coat the inside of a baking tin with fat to help prevent sticking

examples.en: My flatmate showed me how to grease a baking tin for the loaf.
examples.zh: 室友教我怎样「给烤模抹油」，好烤这条面包。

examples.en: I forgot to grease a baking tin before pouring the batter into it.
examples.zh: 我忘了先「给烤模抹油」，就把面糊倒进去了。

collocations: grease a baking tin with butter
grease a baking tin before adding the batter

words.enDefinition: to heat food gently in a container surrounded by hot water

examples.en: The recipe leaves the custard to cook in a water bath in the oven.
examples.zh: 食谱把蛋奶糊放进烤箱「隔水加热烹制」。

examples.en: I watched the pudding cook in a water bath during the baking lesson.
examples.zh: 烘焙课上，我看着布丁「隔水加热烹制」的过程。

collocations: cook in a water bath in the oven
leave custard to cook in a water bath
let the mixture cook in a water bath

words.enDefinition: two stacked pans that use steam from the lower pan to heat food in the upper one

examples.en: I used a double boiler to melt chocolate for our small cakes.
examples.zh: 我用「双层隔水加热锅」融化巧克力，做小蛋糕用。

examples.en: The shared kitchen had a double boiler near the other stainless steel pans.
examples.zh: 共用厨房把「双层隔水加热锅」放在其他不锈钢锅旁边。

collocations: melt chocolate in a double boiler

words.enDefinition: to heat fatty food so the fat melts and can be separated

examples.en: The cook used a separate pan to render the fat from the trimmings.
examples.zh: 厨师用另一个锅，从修切下来的肥肉里「加热炼出脂肪」。

examples.en: The instructor explained that the heat would render the fat during the demonstration.
examples.zh: 老师讲解说，示范中靠加热来「炼出脂肪」。

collocations: render the fat in a pan

words.enDefinition: to cook food slowly with a little liquid, often after browning its surface

examples.en: We planned to braise the cabbage before serving it with mashed potatoes.
examples.zh: 我们打算把卷心菜「用少量汤汁慢焖」，配土豆泥吃。

examples.en: The cook chose to braise the beans with tomatoes and vegetable stock.
examples.zh: 厨师把豆类和番茄用少量高汤「慢焖」。

words.enDefinition: to cook food slowly in liquid, usually with the ingredients cut into pieces

examples.en: I watched my flatmate stew the apples for the crumble we served later.
examples.zh: 我看室友把苹果「用汤汁慢炖」，后来用来做酥粒甜点。

examples.en: The recipe asks us to stew the vegetables before adding the fresh herbs.
examples.zh: 食谱要求，先把蔬菜「用汤汁慢炖」，再加新鲜香草。

words.enDefinition: to cook food for a long time at a low temperature or gentle setting

examples.en: My flatmate planned to slow-cook the vegetables while working on an essay.
examples.zh: 室友打算一边写论文，一边把蔬菜「长时间低温烹煮」。

examples.en: The recipe says to slow-cook the onions so their flavour develops gradually.
examples.zh: 食谱说把洋葱「长时间低温烹煮」，让味道慢慢出来。

words.enDefinition: to cook food in a sealed appliance where steam raises the pressure

examples.en: The cooking class compared how to pressure-cook beans with ordinary stovetop simmering.
examples.zh: 烹饪课对比了怎样「用压力锅烹煮」豆类，以及普通炉灶慢煮的做法。

examples.en: The recipe notes that some cooks pressure-cook the potatoes before mashing them.
examples.zh: 食谱提到，有些人会先「用压力锅烹煮」土豆，再捣成泥。

words.enDefinition: a meal cooked in a single pot or other main cooking vessel

examples.en: We made a one-pot meal because the shared kitchen had only one burner free.
examples.zh: 共用厨房只空出一个灶眼，所以我们做了「一锅做成的一餐」。

examples.en: The recipe for a one-pot meal included rice, vegetables and a little stock.
examples.zh: 这份「一锅做成的一餐」的食谱用到米、蔬菜和一点高汤。

words.enDefinition: in British cooking, a savoury dish made by baking several ingredients together on one tray

examples.en: We made a traybake with potatoes and peppers for our midweek dinner.
examples.zh: 周中晚饭，我们做了「一盘烤成的菜」，里面有土豆和甜椒。

examples.en: I chose a traybake because I could put everything on one oven tray.
examples.zh: 我选了「一盘烤成的菜」，因为所有食材都能放在同一个烤盘上。

words.enDefinition: to start cooking food while it is still frozen

examples.en: The package says to cook from frozen when preparing these vegetables.
examples.zh: 包装上说，这些蔬菜要「不解冻直接烹调」。

examples.en: Before opening the bag, I checked whether the label said to cook from frozen.
examples.zh: 我开袋前确认了标签是否写着要「不解冻直接烹调」。

collocations: follow directions to cook from frozen

words.enDefinition: to heat food on a stove's upper cooking surface rather than inside an oven

examples.en: I decided to cook on the hob because someone else was using the oven.
examples.zh: 因为有人在用烤箱，我决定「在炉灶上烹煮」。

examples.en: The recipe says to cook on the hob for the first stage.
examples.zh: 食谱说，开始阶段需要「在炉灶上烹煮」。

collocations: cook on the hob over low heat
leave the sauce to cook on the hob
suitable to cook on the hob

words.zhGloss: 用微波炉最高功率加热
words.enDefinition: to use the strongest heating setting on a microwave for the food
acceptedZhAnswers: 用微波炉最高功率加热

examples.en: The rice packet says to microwave on full power for the time shown.
examples.zh: 米饭包装说，按标示的时间「用微波炉最高功率加热」。

examples.en: I checked what the instruction to microwave on full power meant for this appliance.
examples.zh: 我核实了这台机器上「用微波炉最高功率加热」的具体含义。

collocations: microwave on full power according to the packet
microwave on full power as directed
instructions to microwave on full power

words.enDefinition: to cook food in an appliance that circulates very hot air around it

examples.en: I decided to air-fry the potato wedges for our lunch in the flat.
examples.zh: 我决定「用空气炸锅烹调」薯角，在住处当午饭。

examples.en: The recipe says you can air-fry the vegetables instead of roasting them in a large oven.
examples.zh: 食谱说，可以「用空气炸锅烹调」蔬菜，不必用大烤箱烤。

words.enDefinition: the removable container that holds the food in an air fryer

examples.en: I let the air-fryer basket cool before removing it from the shared appliance.
examples.zh: 我等「空气炸锅炸篮」凉下来，再把它从共用的机器里取出。

examples.en: The instructions said to place the wedges in the air-fryer basket without piling them up.
examples.zh: 说明说，把薯角放进「空气炸锅炸篮」，不要堆在一起。

collocations: put food in the air-fryer basket

words.enDefinition: to become cooked all the way to the centre of the food

examples.en: The largest potato took longer to cook through than the smaller ones.
examples.zh: 最大的土豆比其他小土豆更久才「熟透」。

examples.en: I checked whether the largest dumpling had enough time to cook through.
examples.zh: 我看了下最大的饺子有没有足够的时间「熟透」。

words.enDefinition: a warm yellow-brown colour developed on food during cooking

examples.en: The top of the bread turned golden brown while we were setting the table.
examples.zh: 我们摆餐具时，面包顶部变成了「金褐色」。

examples.en: I took the biscuits out after their edges became golden brown in the oven.
examples.zh: 饼干边缘在烤箱里变成「金褐色」后，我把它们拿了出来。

words.enDefinition: having firm, brittle edges while the centre may be softer

examples.en: The potato cakes became crisp around the edges but stayed soft inside.
examples.zh: 土豆饼「边缘酥脆」，里面还是软的。

examples.en: I liked the biscuits best when they were crisp around the edges.
examples.zh: 我最喜欢吃「边缘酥脆」的饼干。

collocations: bake until crisp around the edges

words.enDefinition: to become firm and brittle on the surface when heated

examples.en: I waited for the potato skins to crisp up before taking the tray out.
examples.zh: 我等土豆皮「变脆」后，才把烤盘拿出来。

examples.en: The recipe says the bread will crisp up as the surface dries.
examples.zh: 食谱说，面包表面变干时就会「变脆」。

words.enDefinition: soft enough for a fork to go through with little resistance

examples.en: The potatoes were fork-tender when I checked them at the end of cooking.
examples.zh: 我在煮到最后检查土豆时，它们已经「能用叉子轻松扎透」。

examples.en: The roasted carrots were fork-tender, with a little colour on their edges.
examples.zh: 烤胡萝卜「用叉子能轻松扎透」，边缘还有点上色。

words.enDefinition: cooked so softly that the pieces can separate with very little pressure

examples.en: The onions were fall-apart tender after cooking slowly in the covered pan.
examples.zh: 洋葱在盖着盖子的锅里慢慢煮过后，「软烂到轻碰就散」。

examples.en: The slow-cooked squash was fall-apart tender by the time we served dinner.
examples.zh: 端上晚饭时，慢炖的南瓜已经「软烂到轻碰就散」。

words.enDefinition: a consistency that breaks naturally into thin layers or flakes

examples.en: The pastry had a flaky texture around the edges after it cooled.
examples.zh: 酥皮放凉后，边缘呈现「层层易剥开的口感」。

examples.en: The cook described how the baked fish developed a flaky texture without drying out.
examples.zh: 厨师解释烤鱼怎样在不变干的情况下，呈现「一片片易剥开的口感」。

words.enDefinition: to heat food until it changes from opaque to partially transparent

examples.en: The recipe says to cook until translucent before adding the rice to the pan.
examples.zh: 食谱说，先把配料「炒至半透明」，再把米加进锅里。

examples.en: The instructor told us that the onions should cook until translucent without turning brown.
examples.zh: 老师说，洋葱要「炒至半透明」，不要变褐。

collocations: cook until translucent over low heat

words.enDefinition: cooked so that it is still slightly firm to the bite, especially pasta

examples.en: I checked whether the pasta was al dente before pouring off the water.
examples.zh: 把水倒掉前，我尝了尝意面是不是「熟而有嚼劲」。

examples.en: The café served the penne al dente with a vegetable sauce on top.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆的斜管面「熟而有嚼劲」，上面浇了蔬菜酱。

words.enDefinition: a consistency requiring repeated chewing rather than breaking or melting easily

examples.en: These cookies had a chewy texture even after cooling on the rack.
examples.zh: 这些曲奇在晾架上放凉后，口感还是「有嚼劲」。

examples.en: The bread had a chewy texture that worked well for toasted sandwiches.
examples.zh: 这种面包「口感有嚼劲」，做烤三明治很合适。

words.enDefinition: to return to the original shape after light pressure is removed

examples.en: The top of the cake should spring back when gently touched.
examples.zh: 轻轻碰一下蛋糕表面，它应该「受压后回弹」。

examples.en: I saw the dough spring back after my flatmate pressed it lightly.
examples.zh: 室友轻轻按了下面团，我看到它「受压后回弹」。

words.enDefinition: to become firm enough in the centre to hold its shape

examples.en: The custard needed more time to set in the middle before we served it.
examples.zh: 蛋奶冻还需要一点时间让「中心凝固」，再端上桌。

examples.en: I waited for the filling to set in the middle before slicing the pie.
examples.zh: 我等馅料「中心凝固」后，才切开派。

collocations: allow the filling to set in the middle
begin to set in the middle
check that it has set in the middle

words.enDefinition: to move gently from side to side while remaining soft or flexible

examples.en: The centre of the pudding should wobble slightly when we move the dish.
examples.zh: 移动盘子时，布丁的中心应该「轻微晃动」。

examples.en: I could see the custard wobble slightly when my flatmate lifted the tray.
examples.zh: 室友抬起烤盘时，我能看到蛋奶冻「轻微晃动」。

collocations: allow the mixture to wobble slightly
look for the centre to wobble slightly

words.enDefinition: to boil or simmer a sauce so some liquid evaporates and its flavour concentrates

examples.en: My flatmate showed me how to reduce a sauce without scorching the bottom.
examples.zh: 室友教我怎样「收浓酱汁」，同时避免锅底煮焦。

examples.en: The instructor demonstrated how to reduce a sauce at the end of cooking.
examples.zh: 老师示范了烹调接近尾声时怎样「收浓酱汁」。

collocations: reduce a sauce over gentle heat
reduce a sauce to a glaze

words.enDefinition: to increase the thickness of a sauce, for example by adding a thickener

examples.en: The demonstration compared two ways to thicken a sauce for the same dish.
examples.zh: 演示对比了给同一道菜「让酱汁变稠」的两种方法。

examples.en: I used a little cornstarch to thicken a sauce made with vegetable stock.
examples.zh: 我放了一点玉米淀粉，「让蔬菜高汤做的酱汁变稠」。

collocations: use flour to thicken a sauce

words.enDefinition: to make a sauce less thick by adding a suitable liquid

examples.en: I used a little stock to thin a sauce that had reduced too far.
examples.zh: 酱汁收得太浓了，我加了一点高汤来「把酱汁调稀」。

examples.en: The cook explained when to thin a sauce so it still coated the pasta.
examples.zh: 厨师说明了什么时候「把酱汁调稀」，仍能裹在意面上。

collocations: add stock to thin a sauce

words.enDefinition: to keep mixing something without pausing during a particular part of cooking

examples.en: The recipe says to stir constantly while the thick mixture is heating.
examples.zh: 食谱说，浓稠的混合物加热时要「不断搅拌」。

examples.en: I needed to stir constantly because the sauce was starting to stick.
examples.zh: 酱汁开始粘锅了，我需要「不断搅拌」。

words.enDefinition: to mix something from time to time while it is cooking

examples.en: The soup recipe says to stir occasionally while the vegetables soften in the pot.
examples.zh: 汤的食谱说，锅里的蔬菜煮软过程中要「不时搅拌」。

examples.en: I asked my flatmate to stir occasionally while I cleared the table.
examples.zh: 我收拾桌子时，请室友「不时搅拌」一下。

collocations: allow to simmer and stir occasionally

words.enDefinition: to pass a sauce through a fine filter to remove solid pieces

examples.en: I used a fine sieve to strain a sauce before pouring it into bowls.
examples.zh: 我用细筛「过滤酱汁」，再把它倒入碗里。

examples.en: The chef showed us how to strain a sauce so it looked smooth.
examples.zh: 厨师示范了怎样「过滤酱汁」，让它看起来均匀细腻。

collocations: strain a sauce through a sieve
use a sieve to strain a sauce

words.enDefinition: to evaporate enough liquid to leave about half its original volume

examples.en: The recipe says the mixture should reduce by half before we season it.
examples.zh: 食谱说，混合液要「收汁至原量一半」再调味。

examples.en: I marked the original level so I could see the broth reduce by half.
examples.zh: 我标了原来的液面，这样能看出高汤有没有「收汁至原量一半」。

collocations: allow stock to reduce by half
let the sauce reduce by half

words.enDefinition: a sauce whose ingredients have separated instead of remaining blended together

examples.en: The instructor showed an example of split sauce with oil floating on top.
examples.zh: 老师展示了一份油浮在表面的「油水分离的酱汁」。

examples.en: I started over after noticing the split sauce in my small saucepan.
examples.zh: 我发现小锅里是「油水分离的酱汁」，就重新做了一份。

words.enDefinition: the outer edges of food that have darkened or blackened from strong heat

examples.en: I liked the charred edges on the peppers we grilled for the sandwiches.
examples.zh: 我喜欢夹三明治的烤甜椒上「焦黑的边缘」。

examples.en: The vegetables had charred edges while their centres stayed soft and sweet.
examples.zh: 这些蔬菜的「边缘焦黑」，里面还是软甜的。

words.enDefinition: to expose something to strong heat so part of its surface turns black

examples.en: The cook used the grill to char the outside of the sweet peppers.
examples.zh: 厨师用烤架「使甜椒表面焦黑」。

examples.en: The high heat can char the edges before the centre has softened.
examples.zh: 热量很高时，会在中心还没软之前「使边缘焦黑」。

words.enDefinition: cooked too long or at too much heat, reducing the desired quality

examples.en: The green beans were overcooked, so they broke apart when I moved them.
examples.zh: 四季豆「烹煮过头」了，一挪动就断开。

examples.en: I realized the pasta was overcooked when the pieces stopped holding their shape.
examples.zh: 面条不成形了，我才发现已经「烹煮过头」。

words.enDefinition: unpleasantly soft and lacking a clear shape or texture

examples.en: The rice turned mushy after sitting in too much liquid for too long.
examples.zh: 米饭在太多水里放得太久，变得「软烂成糊」。

examples.en: I did not like the carrots once they became mushy in the stew.
examples.zh: 胡萝卜在炖菜里变得「软烂成糊」后，我就不爱吃了。

words.enDefinition: sticky and somewhat rubbery in a way that can make food hard to chew

examples.en: The middle of the loaf was gummy even though the outside looked done.
examples.zh: 面包表面看着已经好了，里头却「黏韧得难嚼」。

examples.en: The noodles became gummy after I left them sitting in a crowded bowl.
examples.zh: 面条放在装得太满的碗里一会儿后，变得「黏韧得难嚼」。

words.enDefinition: heat that remains after the source has been switched off or removed

examples.en: The residual heat softened the cheese after I took the dish from the oven.
examples.zh: 我把盘子从烤箱拿出后，「余热」使奶酪变软。

examples.en: I used the residual heat in the pot to finish melting the butter.
examples.zh: 我利用锅里的「余热」把黄油彻底融化了。

words.enDefinition: continued cooking caused by heat already present in food after the heat source is removed

examples.en: The instructor used a roasted vegetable to demonstrate how carryover cooking changes the texture.
examples.zh: 老师用烤蔬菜示范了「离火后继续熟化」会怎样改变口感。

examples.en: I read about carryover cooking while comparing two recipes for the same roast.
examples.zh: 我比较同一道烤菜的两份食谱时，读到了「离火后继续熟化」。

collocations: carryover cooking after removing food from heat

words.enDefinition: to let cooked meat sit briefly before cutting or serving it

examples.en: The recipe said to rest the meat while we made a quick sauce.
examples.zh: 食谱说，快手酱汁制作期间要「静置熟肉」。

examples.en: The instructor explained why cooks often rest the meat before carving a roast.
examples.zh: 老师说明了为什么厨师通常切烤肉前会先「静置熟肉」。

collocations: allow time to rest the meat

words.enDefinition: to let food lose heat on an open rack that allows air to circulate

examples.en: I left the small cakes to cool on a rack by the window.
examples.zh: 我让小蛋糕「放在晾架上冷却」，架子就搁在窗边。

examples.en: The recipe says the biscuits should cool on a rack before being packed.
examples.zh: 食谱说，饼干打包前应该「放在晾架上冷却」。

collocations: leave cakes to cool on a rack
let bread cool on a rack
allow to cool on a rack

words.enDefinition: to move the cooked food or another item from its container to a plate

examples.en: The recipe says to transfer to a plate after the first batch browns.
examples.zh: 食谱说，第一批上色后就「移到盘子里」。

examples.en: It was easier to transfer to a plate after loosening the edge first.
examples.zh: 先把边缘松开之后，更容易「移到盘子里」。

collocations: transfer to a plate with a spatula
transfer to a plate before serving

words.enDefinition: to offer the food to eat as soon as it is ready

examples.en: The recipe says to serve immediately so the toast stays crisp underneath.
examples.zh: 食谱说要「做好就端上桌」，这样吐司底面还脆。

examples.en: We decided to serve immediately because everyone was already sitting at the table.
examples.zh: 大家已经坐在餐桌旁，我们决定「做好就端上桌」。

words.enDefinition: to offer food while it is still pleasantly warm

examples.en: The instructions say to serve warm with a spoonful of plain yogurt.
examples.zh: 说明里写着配一勺原味酸奶，「温热时端上桌」。

examples.en: I chose to serve warm rolls alongside the soup for our guests.
examples.zh: 我选了「端上温热的」面包卷，和汤一起招待客人。

words.enDefinition: to serve food or drink after it has been cooled in a refrigerator

examples.en: The recipe says to serve chilled once the berry mixture has cooled completely.
examples.zh: 食谱说，浆果混合物完全凉透后，再「冰凉时端上桌」。

examples.en: We planned to serve chilled, so the dessert went into the refrigerator earlier.
examples.zh: 我们打算「冰凉时端上桌」，所以甜点早些时候就放进冰箱了。

words.enDefinition: to change the amount of salt, spices or other flavourings after tasting

examples.en: I stopped to adjust the seasoning before taking the soup to the table.
examples.zh: 把汤端上桌前，我停下来「调整调味」。

examples.en: We tasted the dressing together before deciding how to adjust the seasoning.
examples.zh: 我们一起尝了调味汁，才决定怎样「调整调味」。

words.enDefinition: the way different flavours complement each other without one overpowering the others

examples.en: The instructor asked us to describe the flavour balance of the dressing.
examples.zh: 老师让我们描述调味汁的「风味平衡」。

examples.en: A little lemon changed the flavour balance of the soup we made.
examples.zh: 加了一点柠檬，就改变了汤里各类「风味平衡」。

words.enDefinition: to add fresh herbs at the last stage of preparing a dish

examples.en: The recipe says to finish with fresh herbs just before serving the soup.
examples.zh: 食谱说，汤上桌前要「出锅时加新鲜香草」。

examples.en: We decided to finish with fresh herbs from the pots outside our window.
examples.zh: 我们决定「出锅时加新鲜香草」，用的是窗外花盆里种的。

collocations: finish with fresh herbs before serving
choose to finish with fresh herbs
finish with fresh herbs for freshness

words.enDefinition: to add a small decorative or flavourful item to food before serving

examples.en: I used chopped parsley to garnish the soup before bringing it to the table.
examples.zh: 我用切碎的欧芹「点缀」这道汤，再把汤端上桌。

examples.en: The instructor showed us how to garnish the plate with thin cucumber slices.
examples.zh: 老师示范了怎样用黄瓜薄片「点缀菜品」。

words.enDefinition: to pour a thin stream of oil over food

examples.en: The recipe says to drizzle with oil just before serving the soup.
examples.zh: 食谱说，汤快上桌时「淋上少量油」。

examples.en: I chose to drizzle with oil after arranging the tomatoes on the plate.
examples.zh: 我把番茄摆到盘子上后，选择「淋上少量油」。

collocations: drizzle with oil and lemon juice

words.enDefinition: making a large amount of food at once for several later meals

examples.en: We tried batch cooking on Sunday so weekdays would be less rushed.
examples.zh: 周日我们试了「批量烹调」，这样工作日就不用那么赶。

examples.en: The shared kitchen had enough space for batch cooking with two large pots.
examples.zh: 共用厨房空间足够，能用两个大锅「批量烹调」。

words.enDefinition: to prepare food before the time when it will be needed or served

examples.en: The sauce was easy to make ahead for our evening group dinner.
examples.zh: 为晚上聚餐，可以很方便地把酱汁「提前做好」。

examples.en: I chose a dessert that I could make ahead before my class.
examples.zh: 我挑了一种能在上课前「提前做好」的甜点。

collocations: a dish you can make ahead
choose a recipe to make ahead

words.enDefinition: to tip a baked item out of its tin and onto a rack

examples.en: The recipe says to turn out onto a rack after the tin cools.
examples.zh: 食谱说，等烤模凉下来后，要「脱模倒在晾架上」。

examples.en: I waited a few minutes before trying to turn out onto a rack.
examples.zh: 我等了几分钟，才试着「脱模倒在晾架上」。

collocations: carefully turn out onto a rack
leave briefly before you turn out onto a rack
turn out onto a rack to cool

words.enDefinition: to cover the inside of a baking tin with paper or another lining

examples.en: The recipe says to line the tin before making the brownie mixture.
examples.zh: 食谱说，制作布朗尼面糊之前，要「给烤模铺纸」。

examples.en: I used a small sheet of parchment to line the tin for baking.
examples.zh: 我用一小片烘焙纸「给烤模铺纸」，准备烘烤。

words.enDefinition: a thick heat-retaining slab on which pizza is baked to crisp its base

examples.en: I used a pizza stone when making flatbread for our weekend lunch.
examples.zh: 做周末午饭的薄饼时，我用了「比萨烘烤石板」。

examples.en: The shared kitchen stores the pizza stone in a cupboard beneath the oven.
examples.zh: 共用厨房把「比萨烘烤石板」放在烤箱下面的柜子里。

words.enDefinition: the firmer outer layer of bread or another baked food

examples.en: The bread had a crisp crust even after it had cooled completely.
examples.zh: 面包完全放凉之后，「外皮」仍很酥脆。

examples.en: I liked the dark crust on the loaf we bought for lunch.
examples.zh: 我喜欢午饭买的面包上那层深色的「烘烤形成的外皮」。

words.enDefinition: a bread interior with relatively large, irregular air spaces

examples.en: The loaf had an open crumb that was visible as soon as we cut it.
examples.zh: 面包一切开，就能看出「内部大孔组织」。

examples.en: The baker showed us what an open crumb looked like in sourdough.
examples.zh: 面包师给我们看了酸面包的「内部大孔组织」是什么样。

words.enDefinition: the rapid expansion of bread dough during the first part of baking

examples.en: The instructor pointed out the oven spring just after we put in the loaves.
examples.zh: 老师在面包刚送入烤箱时，让我们看「入炉后迅速膨胀」的现象。

examples.en: The baker discussed how the cuts on top affected the oven spring.
examples.zh: 面包师谈了表面的割口怎样影响「入炉后迅速膨胀」。

words.enDefinition: to leave shaped yeast dough to rise before baking it

examples.en: I had an hour to proof the dough before the kitchen became busy.
examples.zh: 厨房忙起来之前，我有一小时可以「让面团发酵膨胀」。

examples.en: The recipe shows where to proof the dough after shaping the rolls.
examples.zh: 食谱标明面包卷整形后该放在哪儿「让面团发酵膨胀」。

collocations: proof the dough until it has risen

words.enDefinition: the stage when yeast dough is allowed to rise again after its initial rise

examples.en: My flatmate covered the rolls with a cloth during their second rise.
examples.zh: 面包卷「二次发酵」时，室友用布把它们盖了起来。

examples.en: The recipe allows time for a second rise before the bread goes into the oven.
examples.zh: 食谱在面包进烤箱前留了「二次发酵」的时间。

words.enDefinition: to make shallow cuts on dough to guide expansion during baking

examples.en: The instructor showed how to score the dough before sliding it into the oven.
examples.zh: 老师示范了面团进烤箱之前怎样「在面团表面割口」。

examples.en: I practised how to score the dough on the first loaf I made.
examples.zh: 我用自己做的第一条面包练习怎样「在面团表面割口」。

collocations: use a blade to score the dough

words.enDefinition: with a pan or food no longer over an active source of heat

examples.en: I stirred the cheese into the sauce off the heat before serving.
examples.zh: 我在「离火后」把奶酪搅进酱汁，再端上桌。

examples.en: The recipe says to leave the pan off the heat while adding butter.
examples.zh: 食谱说，要在锅「离火后」加黄油。

collocations: add the butter off the heat
leave the pan off the heat

words.enDefinition: to cover food loosely with foil instead of sealing it around the edges

examples.en: The recipe says to tent with foil while the roasted vegetables rest.
examples.zh: 食谱说，烤蔬菜静置时要「用箔纸松松盖住」。

examples.en: I needed to tent with foil because the top was browning too quickly.
examples.zh: 表面上色太快，所以我得「用箔纸松松盖住」。

collocations: tent with foil near the end of baking

words.enDefinition: to let oil that is no longer needed flow away from cooked food

examples.en: I used a wire rack to drain excess oil from the potato cakes.
examples.zh: 我用金属网架给土豆饼「沥去多余的油」。

examples.en: I let the fritters cool on paper towels to drain excess oil.
examples.zh: 我把炸饼放在厨房纸上晾一会儿，「沥去多余的油」。

collocations: drain excess oil on a rack
drain excess oil on paper towels

words.enDefinition: to heat food until the inside, as well as the outside, is warm

examples.en: I left the rolls in the oven to warm through before lunch.
examples.zh: 我把面包卷留在烤箱里，「把食物热透」再吃午饭。

examples.en: The recipe says the filling should warm through while the crust crisps.
examples.zh: 食谱说，外皮变脆时，里面的馅也应该「热透」。

collocations: allow the food to warm through
give the rolls time to warm through
